lost_in_forest.title: Lost in the forest
steps: Pause and establish your location using your map or GPS.
If you cannot safely find your route, contact local emergency services with your location.
Remain where rescuers can find you unless immediate danger requires moving.

cold_weather.title: Cold weather
steps: Put on dry insulating layers.
Use available shelter to reduce weather exposure.
Contact emergency services if you cannot stay warm.
warnings: Weather and temperature can change while you wait.

water.title: Water shortage
steps: Check your remaining drinking water.
Use appropriate treatment supplies before drinking collected water.
Seek assistance if you cannot obtain safe drinking water.
warnings: Do not assume untreated water is safe.

shelter.title: Emergency shelter
steps: Use a tent, tarp, bivy, or emergency blanket for protection.
Keep yourself and your supplies dry.
Make your location visible to rescuers.
warnings: Temporary shelter does not guarantee protection from severe weather.

fire.title: Fire precautions
steps: Check local fire restrictions before using a fire starter.
warnings: Do not light a fire during high wildfire risk.

navigation.title: Navigation
steps: Use familiar navigation tools to establish your location before moving.
warnings: Uncertain navigation can make rescue more difficult.

signaling.title: Signaling for help
steps: Use a whistle or signal mirror to attract rescuers' attention.
warnings: Conserve batteries when using a light for signaling.

bleeding.title: Minor cuts and bleeding
steps: Wash your hands or use clean gloves if available.
Apply gentle, steady pressure with clean gauze or cloth until bleeding stops.
Rinse a minor cut with clean running water, remove visible loose debris, and cover it with a sterile dressing.
warnings: Do not remove deeply embedded objects or probe a wound.
Call emergency services for severe bleeding, a deep or gaping wound, or bleeding that does not stop with steady pressure.
seek_help_if: The wound is deep, contaminated, caused by a bite, or may need tetanus care.
Redness, swelling, warmth, pus, fever, numbness, or loss of movement develops.

burns.title: Minor burns
steps: Move away from the heat source and remove nearby jewelry or tight items unless stuck to skin.
Cool a minor burn under cool running water for 20 minutes.
Loosely cover the burn with a sterile non-stick dressing or clean plastic wrap.
warnings: Do not use ice, creams, grease, or adhesive dressings, and do not break blisters.
Call emergency services for breathing difficulty, electrical or chemical burns, or large, deep, charred, white, or leathery burns.
seek_help_if: The burn involves the face, neck, hands, feet, genitals, a major joint, or circles a limb.
Pain, redness, swelling, drainage, or fever worsens.

sprain.title: Suspected sprain
steps: Stop using the injured joint and protect it from further strain.
Apply a wrapped cold pack for up to 20 minutes at a time and elevate the limb if comfortable.
Use light compression only if it does not cause numbness, tingling, color change, or more pain.
warnings: Do not force the joint back into position or continue activity through significant pain.
seek_help_if: There is deformity, severe pain, numbness, poor circulation, an open wound, or inability to bear weight.
Symptoms are severe, worsening, or not improving.

hypothermia.title: Suspected hypothermia
steps: Call emergency services; hypothermia can be life-threatening.
Move the person gently to shelter, remove wet clothing, and wrap them in dry insulating layers, including the head.
Warm the center of the body gradually. If fully alert and able to swallow, offer a warm non-alcoholic drink.
warnings: Handle the person gently; do not rub limbs, use direct intense heat, or give alcohol.
If the person is unresponsive and not breathing normally, begin CPR if trained and follow emergency-dispatch instructions.
seek_help_if: Hypothermia is suspected, especially with confusion, drowsiness, slurred speech, poor coordination, or slowing/stopping shivering.

heat_exhaustion.title: Suspected heat exhaustion
steps: Stop activity and move the person to a cool or shaded place.
Loosen excess clothing and cool the skin with water, fanning, or wrapped cold packs at the neck and armpits.
If fully alert and not vomiting, give frequent small sips of cool water or an oral rehydration drink.
warnings: Call emergency services immediately for confusion, collapse, seizure, loss of consciousness, or very hot skin; these may indicate heat stroke.
Do not force fluids into anyone who is confused, vomiting repeatedly, or unable to swallow safely.
seek_help_if: Symptoms worsen, emergency signs appear, or the person does not improve promptly after cooling and fluids.

dehydration.title: Suspected dehydration
steps: Rest in a cool or sheltered place and reduce exertion.
If fully alert and able to swallow, take frequent small sips of safe water or an oral rehydration solution.
Monitor alertness, urination, dizziness, vomiting, and whether symptoms improve.
warnings: Call emergency services for confusion, fainting, seizure, inability to wake, severe weakness, or inability to drink.
Do not force fluids into a person who is confused, unconscious, vomiting repeatedly, or unable to swallow safely.
seek_help_if: Symptoms are severe, worsening, or not improving with rest and fluids.
The person is very young, older, pregnant, or has a significant medical condition.
